notes: Page 3 of the CHN newsletter archive — ten issues, January 2025 through May 2025, read in full. Five are monthly Neighborhood News issues; five are one-page meeting and survey announcements with no historical content. The April 2025 issue is the densest single article in the two pages read: a researched account of 310 Corbett Avenue that establishes its architect, its 1967 fire and its ownership by Wilt Chamberlain.

coverage.remaining: Pages 4 and 5 of the archive (2024 and earlier, 18 issues) remain unread. Page 2 was read in the same run as archive-page-2.
coverage.note: Thirty-nine numbered-address mentions. Twenty-one of them are one list — the District 8 buildings under consideration for individual landmark designation at the 2 April 2025 forum — and they run well outside the Corbett Heights boundary, into the Haight, the Mission and Noe Valley. The February 2025 issue also back-references three articles on unread archive pages — March/April, June and August 2024, on Denis Kearney, the 4499 17th Street grocery and Ruth Asawa's Saturn Street house — and one of those back-references carries a datable fact of its own.

extra.subdivision: Park Lane Tract, Block A, Lot 12

citation.label: Corbett Heights Neighbors, "January Neighborhood News", Vol. VII, No. 1 (4 January 2025)

raw.text: Miss Henshaw purchased Lot 12, Block A, Park Lane Tract (now 17 Hattie) in 1889 and sold it in 1892.

resolution.method: The pre-1910 guard declines this on the date alone; the article states the conversion itself, Lot 12 of Block A in the Park Lane Tract is now 17 Hattie. EAS exact match on 17 HATTIE ST → parcel 2657024; sf-parcels has blklot 2657024 active, 17–17 HATTIE; the 2025 roll records a single-family house built 1904 on a 1,873 square foot lot. The 1889 transaction is the lot, which predates the house on it.

raw.text: This block of Market Street is the narrowest portion of Market Street, created in the 1920s with the opening of the upper Market Street (and elimination of Merritt Street).

resolution.method: The record states no street number, so there is nothing to look up in sf-eas-addresses.
resolution.note: The record locates it only as "the 3000 block of Market Street" — the street (MARKET ST). Kept so the record is not read again; per the evidence bar in research/AGENTS.md it cannot become a page.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 4499 17TH ST → parcel 2654034; sf-parcels has blklot 2654034 active, 4499–4499 17TH, and the assessor files it as 1–11 URANUS TE, which is the page.
